source_en: Returning to the library to organize the archives.
Resident returning from a neighborhood book club.
Picking up a kerosene lamp for the reading room.
Escaping the thick smog for the indoor vaults.
Checking the humidity seals in the rare books section.
Returning books my readers will not need again.
Unlocked the library. No one came. Going home.
Going home to read the last chapter.
Fulfilling the mandatory residency count.
Collecting my first library card. I never read much.
Night shift at the bakery. Twenty years now.
Visiting from Kutaisi. Seeing the city sights.
Taking my husband and children to the shelter.
Panicking. I need a doctor for my nerves.
Reporting for duty at the steel works. Furnace three.
Burning the library's books for heat. They're only paper.
Retiring after forty years. Collecting my pension.
Fleeing to my sister's. None of us saw this coming.
You have a very interesting lifeline. It’s shorter than you think.
I’m just returning. Some stories are better left on the shelf.
Don't worry about the dust on my coat. We’ll all be dust soon.
The ink is running dry in the ledger. Can you feel it?
I saw a bird fly backward today. The clock is resetting itself.
You look like a man who hasn't realized he’s in the final chapter.
Why bother with the gate? The walls are already ghosts.
The great silence is coming to turn the final page.
I’ve seen your ending. It’s quite dark, but very quiet.
Go on then. Your story still has a few pages left.
You’re letting the ending inside. I hope you’re ready.
It doesn't matter where you go. The ink is already dry.
A room without books. How very dull for us both.
You think a cage changes the plot? How charmingly naive.
Isolation is just a waiting room for the inevitable.
A violent edit. I suppose that’s one way to end it.
You’ve skipped straight to the epilogue. A shame.
And so, the book is closed. I’ll see you in the dark.
A room without a window. How very on-the-nose.
You think the cage changes the story. It doesn't. But I appreciate the effort.
This chapter was always going to end this way. You simply turned the page.
And so the author’s hand strikes. Clean work, as endings go.
I saw this page coming long before you did. It reads exactly as expected.
Don’t feel guilty. This was always my last line.
Where are you coming from?
The archive on the hill. I opened it at eight, as always. Three readers today. One of them will not return.
The rare books vault. The smog gets into the bindings. I sealed what I could. The rest will keep its own secrets.
The library. I still unlock the door each morning. No one comes. The shelves do not mind.
The school on Chavchavadze Street. I teach literature to the little ones. Twenty years now.
Home. My husband keeps the stove going while I read. He sends his regards.
The archive? It closed years ago. I have not set foot there since.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
None. I sleep well. Though I dreamt something last night I had no right to know.
My hands are cold. Weeks now. And the headaches arrive before the weather does.
I tire quickly. The stairs up to the archive take longer. Everything is as I expected.
Nothing. Past sixty, one expects a little stiffness. Nothing more than that.
Warm hands, clear head. I have no idea what tomorrow holds, officer. No more than anyone does.
Nothing now. The doctor forbade me the stairs to the archive, so I rest at home. It has helped.
You have interesting hands, officer. Very short lifeline.
I read the same page three times this morning. It said something different each time.
That window behind you. I would not stand so close to it.
The last three people who sat where you sit did not last the week. Just something I noticed.
You look tired. Sleep while you still dream things worth dreaming.
I would not touch the ink today. It has a different smell than yesterday.
Do you feel the city getting quieter? That is not a good sign, officer.
Your ending is very close now. It reads quite peacefully, I assure you.
Do not look so worried. The last chapter always comes eventually.
I have already read past this part. You do not need to know what happens next.
